# secopsctl ti

Threat intel & IOCs (read-only): find/inspect IOCs, browse Mandiant collections

## ti collection

Show one threat collection by id (e.g. report--26-10031441)

```text
secopsctl ti collection <id>
```

## ti collection-matches

Show IoC match counts for threat collections

```text
secopsctl ti collection-matches <collection-alt-name-or-id>...
```

```text
Show IoC match counts for one or more threat collections. Pass GTI/Mandiant
alt names such as CAMP.22.147, or a threat collection resource id from
`ti collections --json` / `iocs related --json`.
```

## ti collections

List threat collections (campaigns/reports/…)

```text
secopsctl ti collections [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | int | 25 | maximum number of collections to return |
| `--order` | string | last_modification_date- | server order key (trailing - sorts descending) |
| `--types` | stringSlice | [campaign,report] | collection types to include (campaign,report,actor,malware,vulnerability); empty for all |

## ti find

Resolve indicator value(s) to IoC records (iocs:find)

```text
secopsctl ti find [value...] [flags]
```

```text
Resolve one or more indicators (hash/domain/IP) to their IoC records. Pass
values as arguments and/or read them from a file (or stdin with `--from-file -`),
one per line (blank lines and # comments skipped). Requests are chunked at
1000 indicators (the endpoint's per-request cap) and the results aggregated.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--from-file` | string | - | read indicators from a file (one per line; '-' for stdin) |
| `--type` | string | - | indicator type: md5\|sha1\|sha256\|domain\|ip (default: auto-detect) |

## ti get

Get one IoC by its resource id (from `ti find`, not the raw value)

```text
secopsctl ti get <ioc-id>
```

## ti related

List threat collections related to an IoC resource

```text
secopsctl ti related <ioc-id> [flags]
```

```text
List campaigns and/or reports related to an IoC resource id. The id is the
resource id from `ti find --json`, not the raw indicator value.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--collection-type` | string | all | related threat collection type: campaign\|report\|all |
| `--limit` | int | 25 | maximum related collections per type (API max 40) |
| `--order` | string | last_modification_date- | server order key |
